newsitem.title: USA: Narrow arb throws Latam crudes into US spotlight.
newsitem.headline: Narrow arb throws Latam crudes into US spotlight.

text.p: A continued narrow transatlantic arbitrage threw Latin American crudes into the U.S. spotlight on Friday, traders said.
Activity was subdued, with North Sea and West African crudes off the map for most U.S. Gulf Coast refiners heading into the weekend.
Many of the recent West African availabilities headed into the Far East, while a few were snapped up in the U.S. market.
"The arb is so tight I don't expect to see much activity," a U.S. buyer said.
The July spread between West Texas Intermediate/Cushing and North Sea Brent was around $1.00-10 a barrel, down 25 cents from Thursday, keeping transatlantic activity at bay.
Colombian crudes assumed fresh prominance as refiners moved to wrap up their July requirements.
Colombia's state oil company Ecopetrol was tendering a 500,000 barrel cargo of Vasconia crude, with bids due late next week.
The company was also in the process of awarding a Cano Limon cargo loading July 20-31.
Finally, Ecopetrol was also negotiating to sell two Cusiana cargos loading July 24-28 and July 28-August 1. It was still unclear whether the cargoes would be co-loaded to the same buyer.
Cusiana cargoes usually hold 550,000 barrels apiece.
Cusiana liftings, currently around seven cargoes per month, are slated to increase to nine or 10 in the August program, industry sources said.
By the end of the year, liftings should rise even further as new production comes on stream.
Current Cusiana flows of around 185,000 barrels per day (bpd) are slated to rise to 320,000 bpd this summer and a peak of at least 500,000 bpd in early 1998.
Elsewhere in Latin America, Brazil's state oil company Petrobras bought one million barrels of Escalante crude loading at the end of July from a U.S. company for $4.80-85 under WTI/Cushing.
